Regardless of who starts at quarterback, Egbuka could struggle against a Panthers defense that's allowed just 29.6 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this year.

roster.name: Drake Maye
roster.outlook: Drake Maye hopes to extend his hot streak to four games when the Patriots face the Bears in Week 7. After throwing just one touchdown in his first three games, Maye has burst out with 10 touchdown passes and a scoring rush over his last three games. He now has his full complement of receivers with A.J. Brown returning from an ankle injury. Chicago has allowed two 300-yard passers and multiple touchdown passes three times to date, giving Maye an opportunity to continue his current form Thursday night.

roster.name: George Kittle
roster.outlook: George Kittle and the 49ers are in Atlanta as they look to stay undefeated in Week 7. He caught five of eight targets for 69 yards and a touchdown during San Francisco's 23-17 win in Week 6. Kittle finished second on the team in receptions, yardage and targets on a night where Brock Purdy attempted just 29 passes. The talented tight end boasts a 26-337-5 line on 36 targets through six outings, and he'll aim to keep rolling versus a Falcons defense tied for 23rd in fantasy points allowed per game (16.0) to the position.

roster.name: Blake Corum
roster.outlook: Blake Corum has developed into a legitimate complementary option in the Rams' backfield to star tailback Kyren Williams, rushing 47 times for 223 yards and a touchdown while adding nine receptions for 91 yards and another score through six games. His 4.7 yards per carry almost equals Williams' 4.9 mark, but the main difference is the touches, as Corum is averaging just 7.8 carries per game compared to Williams' 13.3. Still, Corum faces an encouraging Week 7 matchup against the Raiders, who have surrendered 19.6 fantasy points per game to RBs in 2026, the ninth-worst mark in the NFL.His limited receiving involvement and secondary role make him a touchdown-dependent flex option rather than a dependable weekly starter.

roster.name: KC Concepcion
roster.outlook: KC Concepcion and the Browns visit the Titans in Week 7. He hauled in four of six targets for 37 yards and rushed twice for two yards during Cleveland's 13-10 comeback win in Week 6. The rookie first-round pick led the team in targets, tied for first in receptions, and was second in yardage behind veteran Jerry Jeudy (69). Concepcion will look to deliver more, along with the entire Browns' offense, versus Tennessee's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.9) to WRs.

roster.name: Baker Mayfield
roster.outlook: Baker Mayfield (thumb) will operate as the Buccaneers' signal caller if active for the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Mayfield has been sidelined for Tampa Bay's last three contests, but head coach Todd Bowles told reporters he's "supposed to practice" Wednesday, suggesting he could return Sunday. Before the injury, Mayfield struggled in his first three games, throwing for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while also losing three fumbles. However, he could bounce back against a Panthers defense that's allowed 22.0 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

roster.name: Keenan Allen
roster.outlook: Keenan Allen has turned back the clock over his past three appearances for the Colts, securing 19 of 29 targets for 190 yards and a TD over that span while drawing at least nine targets in every game. The 34-year-old wideout should continue to fill a high-volume role in a Colts WR room that lacks appealing alternatives in the continued absence of Alec Pierce (heel). Allen is a high-floor fantasy WR3 in Week 7 against the Vikings, who are allowing 10 catches for 133 yards per game to WRs. Minnesota's aggressive blitz packages will likely force the Colts into plenty of the quick and short throws on which Allen thrives.

roster.name: Bijan Robinson
roster.outlook: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of the Falcons' offense in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Robinson logged a season-low nine carries in the Week 6 loss to the Bears, as Atlanta was trailing by 24 points in the second half. Despite this, he remained productive when given the opportunities, averaging 6.8 yards per carry. Expect Robinson to bounce back and remain one of fantasy's top running backs in Week 7, as San Francisco's defense has allowed 24.5 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs through five contests.

roster.name: Drake London
roster.outlook: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Despite logging double-digit targets for the third time in his last four games, London recorded just four receptions and 62 yards in the Week 6 loss to the Bears. Since Michael Penix returned from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London has averaged 9.3 targets, 6.3 receptions and 117.5 yards per game, making him one of fantasy's most productive receivers. Even so, London could struggle against a tough 49ers defense in Week 7 that's given up just 28.1 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through five games this season.

roster.name: Nico Collins
roster.outlook: Nico Collins has posted at least 79 scrimmage yards in three of his four appearances this season for the Texans ahead of a Week 7 home game against the Giants. The star wideout can be deployed in his usual spot as a fantasy WR1 for Week 7 while facing a Giants secondary that has done a decent job of suppressing yards from WRs but is tied for the fourth-most TDs allowed to the position with seven. Collins has 24 touchdown receptions in 46 games since the start of the 2023 campaign, including three scores in four games this season as the top target for resurgent QB C.J. Stroud.

roster.name: Tyler Warren
roster.outlook: Tyler Warren sat out the Colts' Week 6 loss to the Titans after being a late addition to the injury report due to a groin injury. If the 2025 first-round pick is cleared to return in Week 7 against the Vikings, he would reclaim his role as a key cog on offense for the Colts and a borderline top-five fantasy TE. Jonathan Taylor has seven of the Colts' 13 offensive TDs this season, and Warren has scored three of the other six while averaging six receptions per game. Minnesota hasn't allowed a TE to score this season while giving up 44 receiving yards per game to the position.

roster.name: D'Andre Swift
roster.outlook: D'Andre Swift could see his workload take a hit as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Swift was inefficient on the ground in Week 6 with 16 carries for 44 yards, but he was able to salvage his outing with two rushing touchdowns and four catches for 26 yards. The veteran has benefited from Kyle Monangai being out the last two weeks with turf toe, especially given that three of his six touchdowns this season have come in that stretch. Whether Monangai plays or not, Swift will face a New England front that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs so far this season.

roster.name: DK Metcalf
roster.outlook: DK Metcalf and the Steelers are in Paris for a Week 7 showdown against the Saints. He caught 11 of 15 targets for 93 yards in Pittsburgh's gritty comeback victory in Week 6. Metcalf led the team in yardage and targets while tying with rookie Germie Bernard (11-87-1) for first in receptions. The 11 catches were a product of game flow with the Steelers playing from behind most of the game, and they were Metcalf's most on the season by far, as he had the same number of receptions over his previous three games combined. He'll look to take advantage of a New Orleans defense that just allowed Malik Nabers to record a 12-165-0 line on 15 targets.

roster.name: Jordan Addison
roster.outlook: Jordan Addison will aim to make a return as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. Addison missed Week 5 against the Saints with a hamstring injury, but he luckily had a bye week of rest. The fourth-year wideout will now need to return to practice if he hopes to suit up in Minnesota's upcoming home game. He'll face an Indianapolis defense that's ranked in the middle against fantasy WRs this year.

roster.name: Brian Robinson Jr.
roster.outlook: Brian Robinson is expected to remain the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Robinson was held to just three touches during the Week 6 loss to the Bears, mostly because of the Falcons large deficit early in the game. On the season, Robinson has rushed 53 times for 211 yards and four touchdowns while catching five of six targets for an additional 30 yards. He could struggle finding the end zone in Week 7, however, as San Francisco's defense has given up just three total touchdowns to RBs through five games.

roster.name: Jason Myers
roster.outlook: Jason Meyers and the Seahawks are back home to face off against the 5-0 Chiefs on Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He went 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and did not attempt a PAT during Seattle's 17-14 overtime loss in Week 6. The missed field goal was his first of the season, giving the 35-year-old a 12-for-13 (92.3%) tally through six games. Meyers and the Seahawks offense could struggle to operate versus a Kansas City defense allowing 16.6 points per game, which is the second-best mark in the league.

roster.name: T.J. Hockenson
roster.outlook: T.J. Hockenson holds a questionable tag heading into Minnesota's Week 7 matchup against the Colts. Hockenson sustained a concussion in the Vikings' Week 5 win over the Saints heading into the bye, so his status is up in the air just two weeks later. The veteran tight end will need to clear protocol if he hopes to get back on the field, and that'll be evident through his practice availability. Indianapolis has ranked in the middle against fantasy TEs so far this campaign.

roster.name: Jordan Love
roster.outlook: Jordan Love will look to keep an electric stretch going as the Packers travel to Detroit in Week 7. Love was solid in another Packers win in Week 6, completing 23 of 41 passes for 276 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT ratio, and he also made some noise on the ground with two rushes for 14 yards and a touchdown. The fourth-year starter has now thrown for more than 275 yards in four of six games this season, and he's thrown two touchdowns in all but one outing. He'll enter another favorable matchup as the Lions have allowed the most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks on the year.

free_agents.name: Eddy Pineiro
free_agents.outlook: Eddy Pineiro and the 49ers are back on the road for a meeting with the 2-4 Falcons in Week 7. He converted his only field-goal attempt but went 2-for-3 on extra-point tries during San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6. Pineiro has been underwhelming despite playing for a 49ers team that scores 29.5 points per game, which is the third-most in the league. He's now 6-for-9 (66.7%) on field goals and 19-for-22 (86.4%) on PATs, and he hasn't attempted more than two FGs since the season opener. Pineiro should remain on fantasy waiver wires with more reliable options available at the position.

free_agents.name: Bo Nix
free_agents.outlook: Bo Nix continues to struggle, failing to throw a touchdown in Week 6 for the first time this season while compiling a season-low 107 passing yards. The third-year quarterback has produced fewer than 6.0 yards per attempt in four straight games, and the Broncos' switch back to Sean Payton as the play-caller hasn't yet sparked the offense. Nix has just seven total touchdowns (six passing and one rushing) against five turnovers through seven games, but he'll get a chance to build some momentum in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that's tied for 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

free_agents.name: Jake Ferguson
free_agents.outlook: Jake Ferguson continues to struggle to find his place in the Dallas offense. Ferguson managed just two catches for 13 yards in the dismal 23-13 loss to the Packers. Ferguson has been held out of the end zone in three-straight games, and has failed to gain even 20 yards receiving in any of those contests. He will look to right the ship in Week 7 versus Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.

free_agents.name: Kirk Cousins
free_agents.outlook: Kirk Cousins is coming off a productive effort in the Raiders' near-upset of the Bills in Week 6, throwing for over 300 yards for the second time in six games and tossing multiple TDs for the fifth time. The veteran quarterback is on pace for his first 4,000-yard, 30-TD campaign since 2021 with the Vikings, but to reach those numbers he would need to keep first overall pick Fernando Mendoza on the bench, which looks increasingly unlikely after three straight losses for Las Vegas. Cousins will remain under center for now, but he faces another tough test in Week 7 against a Rams defense that is second in the league in passing yards per game allowed.

free_agents.name: Dameon Pierce
free_agents.outlook: Dameon Pierce rushed for 35 yards and a touchdown in Saquon Barkley's place last game for the Eagles.  Pierce also caught four balls out of the backfield. If Barkley cannot suit up in Week 7 due to his balky hamstring, Pierce would be facing a Dallas defense that has allowed the most rushing yards in the NFL to date. Per game, the Cowboys are allowing a brutal 149.8 yards on the ground.

free_agents.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Godwin was targeted a season-high eight times during the Week 6 loss to the Steelers, recording four receptions for 37 yards. The veteran wideout ranks second on Tampa Bay in targets (30), receptions (23) and yards (216) through the first six games and could benefit from the potential return of Baker Mayfield (thumb) in Week 7. However, Godwin is in for a tough matchup against a Panthers secondary that's allowed just 5.9 yards per pass attempt this season.

free_agents.name: Hunter Henry
free_agents.outlook: Hunter Henry brings a two-game scoring streak into the Patriots' Week 7 matchup with the Bears. With Drake Maye clicking on all cylinders over the last three weeks (10 touchdown passes), Henry has posted at least three catches and 44 yards during that stretch. Chicago has defended tight ends well for most of the season, but over the last two weeks, an opposing tight end has gone for 60 or more yards, and they've surrendered their first two touchdowns of the year to the position. Henry's volume is steady, giving him a bit more of a reliable floor than high potential.

free_agents.name: Sam Darnold
free_agents.outlook: Sam Darnold and the Seahawks host the Chiefs for Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He completed 27 of 51 pass attempts for 278 yards with no TDs and two INTs while rushing twice for 19 yards. Darnold has now thrown four interceptions over his last two outings while taking five sacks in each, giving him seven INTs in five games this season. It could be another rough night for Darnold in Week 7 against Kansas City's third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (16.3) to QBs.

free_agents.name: Dalton Schultz
free_agents.outlook: Dalton Schultz has exceeded 35 receiving yards just once through Houston's first six games of the season and has yet to score a TD heading into a Week 7 home game against the Giants. He's a secondary option in a Houston passing game that has gotten more production out of its WRs in recent weeks, and Schultz's lack of red-zone involvement compared to other middling TE options makes him an unappealing fantasy play. The Giants have limited TEs to two TDs this season, so Schultz is best left on the bench or waivers since his TD drought is unlikely to end in Week 7.

free_agents.name: Tyjae Spears
free_agents.outlook: Tyjae Spears exceeded three touches in only one of the Titans' last four games while playing through ankle and knee injuries. He can be an effective pass-catcher out of the backfield when at full strength while spelling starter Tony Pollard, but Spears hasn't provided much production while banged up. Another quiet performance from Spears is likely forthcoming in Week 7 against a Browns defense that has allowed just one TD to running backs all season, so he isn't a recommended fantasy play, even in deeper formats.

free_agents.name: Rashid Shaheed
free_agents.outlook: Rashid Shaheed and the Seahawks look to snap a two-game losing streak in Week 7 when the Chiefs pay a visit on Sunday Night Football. He caught five of eight targets for 66 yards while rushing once for two yards during Seattle's overtime loss in Week 6. Shaheed also compiled 77 yards on three kickoff returns and another 39 yards on three punt returns, but he fumbled twice while only losing one. He finished second on the Seahawks in yardage, tied with Cooper Kupp for second in receptions, and was third in targets. Shaheed will look to build on that performance versus Kansas City's top-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (21.2) to WRs.

free_agents.name: Tank Dell
free_agents.outlook: Tank Dell (knee) had his 21-day window to return from IR opened ahead of Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans, and he has a realistic chance of being activated ahead of the Week 7 home game against the Giants after sitting out against the Titans in Week 5 and the Jaguars in Week 6. Even if Dell suits up in Week 7, he's likely to be brought along slowly in a Texans WR room that also has Nico Collins, Marvin Harrison, Jaylin Noel, Xavier Hutchinson, and Kayshon Boutte vying for playing time. Dell is a viable bench stash, but he isn't a recommended starting option against the Giants.

free_agents.name: Jacoby Brissett
free_agents.outlook: Jacoby Brissett will look to build on Arizona's Week 6 victory over the Rams when the Cardinals host the Broncos in Week 7. The veteran quarterback has completed 156 of 234 passes for 1,328 yards, nine touchdowns and six interceptions through six games, averaging 221.3 passing yards per contest. However, his 5.7 yards per attempt are the best example of the struggles Arizona's offense endures to generate explosive passing plays, and Denver represents another challenging opponent. The Broncos have allowed just 14.9 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, the 12th-best mark in the NFL, limiting Brissett's appeal despite his established passing volume. He's best viewed as a lower-end QB2 in superflex formats.

free_agents.name: Jayden Reed
free_agents.outlook: Jayden Reed will remain inactive as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he'll now require season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Savion Williams and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.

free_agents.name: Chase McLaughlin
free_agents.outlook: Chase McLaughlin is expected to remain one of fantasy's top kickers in the Buccaneers' Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. McLaughlin had an impressive showing in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Buccaneers, converting on all four of his field-goal tries, including three from 40-plus yards. The veteran kicker is perfect on the season, making 14 field goals and 11 extra points. He'll likely have multiple scoring opportunities in Week 7, as the Panthers defense has allowed 7.4 kicking points per game this year.

free_agents.name: Michael Mayer
free_agents.outlook: Michael Mayer took advantage of the extra defensive attention the Bills paid to Brock Bowers in Week 6, catching seven of nine targets for a season-high 95 yards. While Bowers remains the top option in the Raiders' passing attack, Mayer is on pace for a career-best year of his own, producing a 28-266-1 line on 34 targets through six games. He is eight receptions and 63 yards away from establishing new personal bests. Mayer will likely struggle to reach those marks in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

free_agents.name: Jameis Winston
free_agents.outlook: Jameis Winston was benched in favor of J.J. McCarthy last game for the Giants. McCarthy led a furious comeback attempt, throwing for an astonishing 243 yards in the fourth quarter alone in relief of Winston. While the G-Men ultimately lost to the Saints by a score of 34-27, McCarthy's near-heroics have likely created a quarterback controversy heading into Week 7 versus the Texans. Whomever lines up under center may have a favorable matchup, as Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.

free_agents.name: Deshaun Watson
free_agents.outlook: Deshaun Watson and the Browns travel to square off against the Titans in Week 7. He completed 16 of 26 pass attempts for 164 yards and rushed eight times for 29 yards during Cleveland's 13-10 win in Week 6. Watson is not much of a fantasy-friendly quarterback, but he has the Browns at 4-2 and tied for first in the AFC North. Next up is a stingy Tennessee defense that ranks 10th in fantasy points allowed per game (18.6) to QBs.

free_agents.name: Adonai Mitchell
free_agents.outlook: Adonai Mitchell will need to overcome a finger injury that cost him four games if he's to help the Jets against the Dolphins in Week 7. Mitchell looked firm in his role opposite Garrett Wilson prior to injury, but it's fair to question his immediate role should he be active in Week 7. Facing a Dolphins' secondary that's surprisingly allowing the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers despite a desirable 8.2 yards per target doesn't profile as a re-emergent spot, especially with Omar Cooper healthy and surging.

free_agents.name: Daniel Jones
free_agents.outlook: Daniel Jones and the Colts are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the previously winless Titans, and things get significantly more difficult on the road in Week 7 against the Vikings, who are allowing a league-low 12.8 points per game. Jones played his part in the loss to Tennessee with a season-worst two interceptions, and he has yet to throw multiple touchdown passes in a game while posting a 4:6 TD:INT through six outings. He's averaging just 215 passing yards and nine rushing yards per game. Even in superflex and multi-QB formats, the struggling QB isn't an advisable fantasy option.

free_agents.name: Mike Gesicki
free_agents.outlook: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Baltimore for an AFC North clash in Week 7. He caught one of two targets for a four-yard touchdown during Cincinnati's 31-24 win in Week 5. Fellow tight end Erick All Jr. notched a 3-25-0 line on three targets, finishing second on the team in yardage. Gesicki is hard to trust with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) healthy, especially versus a Baltimore defense tied for seventh in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to TEs.

free_agents.name: Jaylin Noel
free_agents.outlook: Jaylin Noel has made the most of his opportunities all season, and Houston's 2025 third-round pick has started to earn a larger role in recent weeks. He takes a two-game touchdown streak into Week 7 against the Giants. Noel has caught all 12 of his targets for 233 yards over the past three games after posting five catches for 101 yards on nine targets through Week 3. Nico Collins remains the clear No. 1 option in Houston's passing game, and the role of trade acquisition Marvin Harrison should grow moving forward, but Noel's recent success makes him a viable Week 7 flex play against a Giants secondary that has allowed seven receiving TDs to WRs in six games.

free_agents.name: Emmett Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Emmett Johnson remains stuck in a low-volume role behind Kenneth Walker in the Kansas City backfield. Johnson hasn't logged double-digit touches since Week 1, and his three targets in a Week 6 win over the Chargers were a season-high. The rookie running back will likely need an injury to Walker to contribute. Johnson will look for his first NFL touchdown in Week 7 against a Seahawks defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Trey Smack
free_agents.outlook: Trey Smack will look to build off a solid performance as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. After a disappointing performance even in a blowout victory against the Bears, Smack nailed all three of his field-goal tries and went two-for-two on XPAs in a Week 6 win over Dallas. The rookie kicker has now converted 10 of 13 field-goal kicks and gone 11-for-13 on extra-point attempts this season. He'll face a Detroit defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to kickers.

free_agents.name: Rashod Bateman
free_agents.outlook: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) and the Ravens host the division-rival Bengals in Week 7. He failed to catch his only target before exiting in the second quarter of Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. Bateman sat out the entire second half while dealing with the nagging shoulder issue, allowing rookie Jakobi Lane to rack up a 4-40-0 receiving line on five targets. Even if Bateman is able to suit up against Cincinnati in Week 7, he should remain on fantasy benches due to his inconsistent involvement in the offense, regardless of the Ravens' quarterback situation.

free_agents.name: Darren Waller
free_agents.outlook: Darren Waller is expected to remain the Panthers' primary pass-catching tight end in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Despite going with a catch in Carolina's Week 6 win over the Eagles, Waller still leads the TE corps in targets (18) and yards (148) through five contests. However, Waller will likely see less opportunities to score with Jalen Coker back from injury. Regardless, Waller is in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Tampa Bay defense that's already allowed four receiving touchdowns to TEs this year.

free_agents.name: Michael Penix Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Michael Penix will continue leading the Falcons' offense during the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Penix was productive despite a loss in Week 6, throwing for 225 yards and three touchdowns while also completing two two-point conversions. Since returning from injury, Penix has led the Falcons' offense to 31.5 points per game, the second-most in the NFL during that span. However, he could struggle against a tough 49ers defense that's given up just 16.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks through five contests.

free_agents.name: J.J. McCarthy
free_agents.outlook: J.J. McCarthy led a furious comeback attempt by the Giants last game. Though McCarthy's efforts fell short, he threw for an astonishing 243 yards in the fourth quarter alone in relief of starter Jameis Winston. While the G-Men ultimately lost to the Saints by a score of 34-27, McCarthy's near-heroics have likely created a quarterback controversy heading into Week 7 versus the Texans. Whomever lines up under center may have a favorable matchup, as Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.

free_agents.name: Ryan Flournoy
free_agents.outlook: Ryan Flournoy found the end zone last game for Dallas. Flournoy reeled in seven passes for 40 yards and the score in the 23-13 loss to the Packers. Flournoy has at least four targets in every game this season, though has gone over 40 yards receiving just once. He remains firmly behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens heading into a Week 7 clash with Philly. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.

free_agents.name: Caleb Douglas
free_agents.outlook: Caleb Douglas hopes to emerge from the Dolphins' bye week healthy and help their struggling passing game in Week 7 against the Jets. Douglas hasn't played since Week 2 due to an ankle injury and was used at varying rates when healthy: seven targets in his debut followed by just three the following week. While his 94 yards in Week 1 show potential, uncertain availability and opportunity likely keep him off the radar for lineup consideration against a slightly above-average Jets' secondary that's surrendering 7.3 yards per target.

free_agents.name: Samaje Perine
free_agents.outlook: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to take on the 4-2 Ravens in Week 7. He rushed 14 times for 68 yards and caught both of his targets for 10 yards and a TD during Cincinnati's Week 5 victory. Perine out-carried starter Chase Brown (13) and was much more efficient, as Brown managed just 39 yards on the ground. If Brown continues to struggle, Perine could have a larger role than initially anticipated at the beginning of the campaign. However, it might be wise to wait until we know more about the backfield hierarchy following the matchup against Baltimore's seventh-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.6) to RBs.

free_agents.name: Cooper Kupp
free_agents.outlook: Cooper Kupp and the Seahawks host the 5-0 Chiefs on Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He caught five of 10 targets for 50 yards during Seattle's 17-14 overtime loss in Week 6. Kupp finished behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (16) for second on the team in targets, as his 10 looks from QB Sam Darnold were a season high for the 33-year-old. He'll try to relieve some of the pressure Smith-Njigba will face versus a Kansas City defense that allows 21.2 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks first.

free_agents.name: Geno Smith
free_agents.outlook: Geno Smith will look to buck his seasonal trends in an inviting Week 7 matchup when the Jets face the Dolphins. Smith has opened the year with one or zero touchdown passes in five of his six games, but Miami's defense has allowed 11 touchdown throws in five contests. Smith likely needs those timely scoring plays as Miami is allowing just 226 passing yards per game, with teams preferring to exploit its run defense, setting him up as a risky bye-week replacement option.

free_agents.name: Pierre Strong Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Pierre Strong will look to make the most of his opportunities as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Strong led Green Bay's backfield in a Week 6 win over the Cowboys, rushing the ball 11 times for 28 yards and catching five of six targets for 39 yards. The fourth-year running back looks to be a more dynamic option than MarShawn Lloyd moving forward, but both players could see a diminished role with Josh Jacobs set to return from the Commissioner's Exempt list. Detroit has ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

free_agents.name: Justice Hill
free_agents.outlook: Justice Hill and the Ravens host the Bengals for an AFC North clash in Week 7. He did not record a carry but brought in all three of his targets for nine yards during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. Derrick Henry accounted for 17 of the 18 rushing attempts out of the Ravens' backfield, a trend that should continue as long as he remains healthy. Hill should remain on fantasy benches against a Cincinnati defense that is tied for ninth in fantasy points allowed per game (19.0) to RBs

free_agents.name: Kendrick Bourne
free_agents.outlook: Kendrick Bourne has established himself as a regular contributor in Arizona's passing attack, catching 22 passes for 225 yards through six games, though he hasn't found the end zone. The veteran wideout is averaging a career-low 10.2 yards per catch in 2026, but that's also due to the struggles the Cardinals' passing attack has had with Jacoby Brissett under center. To make things even more complicated, he'll face the Broncos' secondary in Week 7, and Denver has allowed the seventh-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts in 2026. That makes Bourne a difficult player to trust outside deeper PPR leagues.

free_agents.name: Roschon Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Roschon Johnson could be in line for another solid workday again in Week 7 as the Bears play the Patriots. Johnson capitalized on his usage once again with Kyle Monangai (toe) sidelined in Week 6, rushing 13 times for 51 yards and a touchdown and catching two passes for 34 yards. He's now totaled 125 yards and a touchdown on 27 touches in the last two games with Monangai out. If this stays the case, Johnson will be playable against a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs.

free_agents.name: George Holani
free_agents.outlook: George Holani and the Seahawks host the Chiefs on Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He rushed five times for 20 yards and a touchdown during Seattle's 17-14 loss in overtime in Week 6. Holani made the most of his touches by scoring his first rushing TD of the season, but he's expected to have his opportunities reduced with the likely return of Zach Charbonnet (knee) off the reserve/PUP list. It would be wise to steer clear of the Seahawks backfield against a Kansas City defense allowing 19.0 fantasy points allowed per game to RBs, which is tied for ninth.

free_agents.name: Calvin Ridley
free_agents.outlook: Calvin Ridley finished without a catch in three of six games this season for the Titans and has just five receptions for 81 yards overall. The veteran WR has been relegated to a depth role at this stage of his career and can continue to be ignored in fantasy. After improving to 1-5 with a Week 6 win over the Colts, the Titans will host the 4-2 Browns in Week 7.

free_agents.name: Nick Folk
free_agents.outlook: Nick Folk could have plenty of scoring opportunities when the Falcons take on the 49ers in Week  7. Folk converted on his lone point-after attempt in the Week 6 loss to the Bears, with the Falcons converting on two two-point conversions in the second half. On the season, Folk has made nine of 12 field-goal tries and all 13 of his point-after attempts. The veteran kicker is in for a favorable Week 7 matchup as well, with San Francisco's defense giving up 8.6 kicking points per game through five contests this year.

free_agents.name: Malik Willis
free_agents.outlook: Malik Willis hopes to emerge from the Dolphins' bye week with answers to get their offense in gear during a Week 7 matchup with the Jets. He has been held under 200 yards passing in three of his five games and has only two touchdown passes but has shown signs of his dual-threat capability, averaging 47.0 rushing yards over his last three contests. The Jets have allowed the eighth-fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks thus far, surrendering only nine touchdown passes and 92 rushing yards in six games, boding poorly for Willis's chances to shine.

free_agents.name: Chad Ryland
free_agents.outlook: Chad Ryland enters Arizona's Week 7 matchup against Denver following one of the most productive kicking performances of the season. He converted all six field-goal attempts against the Rams, including a game-winning 43-yarder as time expired, accounting for all 18 of the Cardinals' points. Ryland has benefited from an Arizona offense that frequently struggles to finish drives, creating additional field-goal opportunities despite inconsistent touchdown production. However, Denver has allowed just 7.5 fantasy points per game to opposing kickers this season, making the matchup less attractive than his recent performance suggests, but he's a player to keep close tabs on either way. Ryland remains a viable streaming option, but he should continue to be a matchup-based alternative, and fantasy managers shouldn't expect six field goals on a steady basis.

free_agents.name: Jaleel McLaughlin
free_agents.outlook: Jaleel McLaughlin and the Browns are in Tennessee for an interconference tilt in Week 7. He rushed nine times for 41 yards and caught all four targets for another 14 yards during Cleveland's Week 6 win. With Quinshon Judkins (ankle) inactive, McLaughlin and Audric Estime each tallied nine carries to lead the backfield. McLaughlin paced the team in yardage and tied for the lead in receptions. If Judkins can't play against the Titans' 13th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (20.3) to RBs, McLaughlin could find himself busy again.

free_agents.name: Blake Grupe
free_agents.outlook: Los Angeles placed Blake Grupe on injured reserve after he suffered a torn ACL in Week 6 against the Cardinals, and they're expected to work out multiple kickers over the next few days before deciding on a new option prior to Sunday's game against the Raiders in Week 7. Regardless of who gets the nod in Week 7, this might not be a favorable matchup for Rams kickers since the Raiders have given up the 11th-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing kickers in 2026.

free_agents.name: Jake Elliott
free_agents.outlook: Jake Elliott managed just two extra points last game for the Eagles, as the Philadelphia offense sputtered without Jalen Hurts. Tanner McKee lined up under center, and should continue to be the quarterback as Hurts will be sidelined for the season. Even with Hurts at the helm, the Eagles offense had failed to score more than 20 points in each of the previous three contests. Saquon Barkley continues to be sidelined as well. In sum, Elliott's prospects for a plethora of points does not look hopeful, even against a Dallas squad in Week 7 allowing 26.5 points per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Malachi Fields
free_agents.outlook: Malachi Fields finished third on the Giants in targets last game. Fields was targeted eight times, though managed two catches for just 18 yards in the 34-27 loss to the Saints. Fields has emerged as the No. 2 wideout behind Malik Nabers, though Isaiah Likely at tight end has also been extremely busy as a pass catcher. Fields has at least two catches in every game he's played, though has just 12 catches on the season. In Week 7, the Giants will face a porous Texans secondary allowing 246 passing yards per contest, which is 27th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Jaylen Wright
free_agents.outlook: Jaylen Wright hopes to come out of the Dolphins' bye with a larger role in Week 7 against the Jets. Wright has only amassed 11 carries over his last two outings, finishing with 18 yards while not being targeted in the passing game. Ollie Gordon has dominated backfield work since De'Von Achane (knee) went down for the season, leaving managers in a wait-and-see mode with regards to Wright against a defense that's allowing 4.2 yards per carry, ranking near the middle of the pack league-wide.

free_agents.name: Cam Ward
free_agents.outlook: Cam Ward and the Titans finally earned their first win of the season in Week 6 against the Colts, though the second-year QB certainly wasn't the primary driving force in the victory, as he threw for just 102 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT. Ward has mustered just four touchdown passes through six starts in his sophomore season while averaging 166 passing yards per game. He'll face a franchise that's all too familiar with subpar QB play in Week 7, taking on a Browns team that's off to a surprisingly strong 4-2 start this season while boasting one of the league's 10 stingiest defenses in terms of both passing yards and points allowed per game. Between Ward's own shortcomings and the tricky matchup, it's best to avoid him in fantasy for Week 7.

free_agents.name: Wil Lutz
free_agents.outlook: Wil Lutz played hero for the Broncos in Week 6, with his only field goal coming in overtime during a win over the Seahawks. The veteran kicker's volume is inconsistent thanks to Denver's struggling offense, and through six games, he's gone 9-for-12 on FG attempts and a perfect 9-for-9 on extra points. Lutz could be busier than usual in Week 7 against a Cardinals team that's allowed 29.7 points per game, tied with the Saints for the worst mark in the league.

free_agents.name: Tanner McKee
free_agents.outlook: Tanner McKee started last game at quarterback for the Eagles, and he could potentially find himself under center for the foreseeable future. Starter Jalen Hurts will be sidelined for the remainder of the season due to blood clots, leaving McKee as next in line under center. He threw for 215 yards and a touchdown last game versus the Panthers. In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.

free_agents.name: Jalen Nailor
free_agents.outlook: Jalen Nailor returned in Week 6 from a one-game absence due to a concussion, but he was able to turn four targets into just one nine-yard catch. The former Viking remains an afterthought in the Raiders' passing game, and through five contests, he's managed just a 6-61-0 line on 15 targets. Nailor's prospects could improve if Fernando Mendoza replaces Kirk Cousins under center at some point, but he'd likely need injuries to the likes of Brock Bowers or Tre Tucker to be anything more than the No. 4 option for either QB. Nailor isn't likely to break out in Week 7 against a Rams secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Tyler Huntley
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Huntley and the Ravens return home for a divisional clash against the Bengals in Week 7. He completed 19 of 31 pass attempts for 165 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing five times for 28 yards during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. It was an underwhelming day for the Ravens' offense, which accumulated just 252 total yards and scored all 10 of their points in the opening quarter. Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status for Week 7 is still murky at best, meaning Huntley could earn a second straight start against a Cincinnati defense allowing 21.5 fantasy points per game (19th) to QBs.

free_agents.name: Cade Otton
free_agents.outlook: Cade Otton is expected to remain one of Tampa Bay's top pass catchers in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Otton struggled during the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, hauling in one of two targets for four yards. Despite this, he played 100% of the Buccaneers' offensive snaps, suggesting more fantasy production is coming in the near future. Otton is also in for a favorable matchup in Week 7, as Carolina's defense has given up 16.0 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

free_agents.name: Darnell Washington
free_agents.outlook: Darnell Washington and the Steelers are in Paris for an interconference tilt against the Saints in Week 7. He brought in four of six targets for 25 yards and a touchdown during Pittsburgh's thrilling comeback victory in overtime in Week 6. Washington and fellow tight end Pat Freiermuth each played 71% of the offensive snaps, lending more credibility to the "your turn, my turn" trend that's developing in 2026. He'll look to exploit New Orleans' 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.6) to TEs.

free_agents.name: Chris Brooks
free_agents.outlook: Chris Brooks will be out again in Week 7 when the Packers play the Lions. Brooks is currently on IR with an ankle injury, which will keep him out for at least the next two weeks. His absence from the field should continue to give Pierre Strong more opportunities in the run game.

free_agents.name: Jauan Jennings
free_agents.outlook: Jauan Jennings is a depth option ahead of Minnesota's Week 7 matchup against the Colts. Jennings has been unable to get things going so far this season, with just two catches for nine yards across his four appearances. The only positive outlook moving forward for the veteran is that he's been on the field for a favorable number of offensive snaps, but that hasn't translated into output. Indianapolis has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.

free_agents.name: Dohnte Meyers
free_agents.outlook: Dohnte Meyers and the Bengals visit the division-rival Ravens in Week 7. He caught both of his targets for 12 yards during Cincinnati's Week 5 victory. With Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) both healthy, Meyers returned to a supporting role, supplying 91 yards on three kick returns and another 13 yards on two punt returns. Rookie Colbie Young (knee) could also return from a two-game absence, so both receivers could struggle to make much of a contribution against the Ravens' 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (34.1) to the position.

free_agents.name: Xavier Hutchinson
free_agents.outlook: Xavier Hutchinson had season-low totals across the board with two catches for 10 yards on three targets in Houston's Week 6 win over the Jaguars, and he won't be a recommended Week 7 fantasy play against the Giants, even in deeper formats. He was earning decent volume while Houston's WR room was banged up, but the return of Nico Collins from a hamstring injury, coupled with the trade for Marvin Harrison and emergence of Jaylin Noel, have relegated Hutchinson to a depth role. Hutchinson doesn't have the talent to find consistent success with limited usage, as he has just three TDs in 55 career regular-season games.

free_agents.name: Efton Chism III
free_agents.outlook: Efton Chism's role in the Patriots passing game is in doubt ahead of a Week 7 matchup with the Bears. With A.J. Brown returning from an ankle injury in Week 6, Chism only had one target after compiling 10 looks over the past two weeks. That low volume came with Romeo Doubs missing three quarters of action as well, so even if Doubs misses Week 7, Chism will still have limited opportunities to best a secondary that's allowing 9.8 yards per target, the third-highest mark in the league.

free_agents.name: Colby Parkinson
free_agents.outlook: Colby Parkinson operates as the Rams' main blocking tight end, and while he's going to have a few catches here and there, he's behind Tyler Higbee in terms of the pecking order in the passing game. The matchup is favorable against the Raiders, who have allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing TEs in 2026, but Parkinson's lack of involvement will limit his upside overall. He has just nine catches for 55 yards and a touchdown in five games this season.

free_agents.name: Jahan Dotson
free_agents.outlook: Jahan Dotson is expected to remain the Falcons' No. 2 wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Dotson had his most productive outing of the 2026 season in the Week 6 loss to the Bears, catching three of five targets for 87 yards and a touchdown. On the season, he's caught 11 of 23 targets for 236 yards and two touchdowns, benefitting from the return of quarterback Michael Penix. However, Dotson could struggle against the 49ers in Week 7, as they have allowed just 5.7 yards per pass attempt through five games this season.

free_agents.name: Evan Engram
free_agents.outlook: Evan Engram continues to see little usage in the Broncos' offense. Despite quarterback Bo Nix's struggles to attack downfield, Engram isn't getting much volume as a check-down option, failing to see more than five targets in any game this season and amassing a 12-134-1 line on 19 targets through six contests. Even if Nix picks up the pace, Engram likely won't be much of a factor. The veteran tight end does get a favorable matchup in Week 7 against a Cardinals defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to the position.

free_agents.name: Gunnar Helm
free_agents.outlook: Gunnar Helm has been trending in the wrong direction, with consecutive zero-catch performances coming into a Week 7 home game against the Browns and just nine catches for 60 yards all season. He continues to lead Tennessee's TEs in playing time, but Helm has been used almost exclusively as a blocker in recent weeks. Helm remains a non-factor for fantasy purposes in Week 7.

free_agents.name: Isaac TeSlaa
free_agents.outlook: Isaac TeSlaa will aim to bounce back as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. After it appeared the second-year pass catcher was starting to carve out a role for himself again, TeSlaa recorded zero catches against the Cardinals before Detroit's bye. Hopefully the second game this year with zero catches was another anomaly, as there is plenty of love to spread with the Lions' high-volume offense. Green Bay has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.

free_agents.name: Brandin Cooks
free_agents.outlook: Brandin Cooks and the 49ers are back on the road for a meeting with the Falcons in Week 7. He brought in one of two targets for 13 yards during San Francisco's Week 6 win. With Mike Evans expected to miss time after aggravating his Achilles injury in the victory and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) in jeopardy of missing a second straight game, Cooks could see an uptick in opportunities. However, there's a possibility of Christian Kirk (calf/IR) making his debut for the 49ers, which would hinder some of Cooks' value versus an Atlanta defense allowing 37.0 fantasy points per game (27th) to WRs.

free_agents.name: Chris Bell
free_agents.outlook: Chris Bell will look for a bigger role in the Dolphins' passing game coming out of a bye in Week 7 against the Jets. He has failed to record a catch in three of his first five games to start his career, with Miami's production failing to reach 200 yards. With the Jets allowing just 202 passing yards per game and Bell logging a limited workload, he's unlikely to garner Week 7 fantasy attention.

free_agents.name: Daniel Carlson
free_agents.outlook: Daniel Carlson could have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Saints' Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Carlson's struggles continued in the Week 6 win over the Giants, missing a kick for the fourth consecutive week. On the season, he's made seven of 10 field-goal tries and 15 of 17 point-after attempts. Despite the inconsistency, he's in for a very favorable Week 7 matchup against a Steelers defense that's allowed 10.3 kicking points per game this season, tied for the most in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Andy Borregales
free_agents.outlook: Andy Borregales hasn't been a huge scorer despite the Patriots' offensive uptick over the last three weeks as they get set to face the Bears in Week 7. While he's garnered 12 PATs in this stretch, the offensive efficiency has resulted in just three field goal tries, all from inside 40 yards. Chicago has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing kickers, so until the Patriots' offense slows down and Borregales gets more field goal attempts, his fantasy viability appears minimal.

free_agents.name: Zachariah Branch
free_agents.outlook: Zachariah Branch's offensive role could continue to grow as the Falcons' face the 49ers in Week 7. Branch has caught all six of his targets over the last three weeks, accumulating 34 receiving yards. He appears to have emerged as Atlanta's No. 3 wideout, as Olamide Zaccheaus hasn't caught a pass since the Week 3 win over the Packers. Regardless, Branch will likely struggle in Week 7, as San Francisco's defense has given up just 8.9 yards per completion through five games this season.

free_agents.name: Jalon Daniels
free_agents.outlook: Jalon Daniels is expected to start at quarterback if Baker Mayfield (thumb) remains sidelined for the Buccaneers' Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Daniels struggled against the Steelers defense in a Week 6 overtime loss, throwing for 164 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions while adding 39 yards on nine carries. Over his first three NFL starts, Daniels has accounted for just three touchdowns and five turnovers, suggesting he'll carry minimal fantasy value going forward. Despite this, Daniels could be in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Carolina defense that's given up 146 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns to quarterbacks this season.

free_agents.name: Konata Mumpfield
free_agents.outlook: Konata Mumpfield enters Week 7 with an opportunity to expand his role in the Rams' passing attack after Davante Adams suffered a significant hamstring injury that will sideline him for multiple weeks. Mumpfield has caught eight passes for 127 yards and a touchdown through six games, averaging an impressive 15.9 yards per reception despite limited opportunities. His ability to generate explosive plays could make him a useful complement to Puka Nacua, but his fantasy upside will be boom-or-bust, as he's likely to operate as a touchdown-dependent option with other names ahead of him in the pecking order. At least the Week 7 matchup against the Raiders is favorable, as Las Vegas has allowed the 10th-most receiving yards and fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts in 2026.

free_agents.name: KaVontae Turpin
free_agents.outlook: KaVontae Turpin left the last game for the Cowboys due to a rib injury, leaving his status in question for Week 7 versus the Eagles. Tyler Goodson handled kick return duties, while Jonathan Mingo caught punts in Turpin's absence. His targets on offense appear to have been gobbled up by No. 3 wideout Ryan Flournoy. If Turpin can return in Week 7, he would face an Eagles defense allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Andre Szmyt
free_agents.outlook: Andre Szmyt and the Browns visit the Titans for a Week 7 showdown. He made two of his three field-goal attempts, including the 48-yard game-winner, and his lone PAT during Cleveland's 13-10 win in Week 5. It was Szmyt's first field goal miss this season, as he's now 12-for-13 (92.3%) through six games. The Browns' offense has taken a step back in recent weeks, scoring a combined 22 points in their last two outings, leaving Szmyt a difficult kicker to rely on in fantasy.

free_agents.name: Jalen Royals
free_agents.outlook: Jalen Royals recorded a career-high four targets in Kansas City's Week 6 win over the Chargers, catching two for 24 yards. The second-year wideout's role has slightly increased with Rashee Rice sidelined, but Royals still has yet to prove himself as a trusted option for Patrick Mahomes. Even if Rice remains on the shelf in Week 7, Royals isn't likely to break out against a Seahawks secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Savion Williams
free_agents.outlook: Savion Williams will aim to stay involved as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Williams got plenty of usage in his season debut versus the Cowboys in Week 6, catching all four of his targets for 32 yards and rushing the ball twice for nine yards. The second year looks to be the WR3 behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, especially given that Skyy Moore is on IR with an ankle injury. Williams will face a Detroit defense that's ranked 30th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Darnell Mooney
free_agents.outlook: Darnell Mooney sustained a neck injury in the second half of the last game for the Giants. Mooney did not record a catch prior to his exit, though did manage a 20-yard rush. Mooney has struggled in his first season with the Giants, recording just eight catches for 109 yards on the season. It remains to be seen if he will be able to suit up in Week 7 versus the Texans. If he can play, Mooney would face a Texans defense allowing 246 passing yards per clash, which is 27th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Greg Dulcich
free_agents.outlook: Greg Dulcich is facing an uphill battle for meaningful production when the Dolphins face the Jets in Week 7. Dulcich's usage has been sporadic, notching 12 targets in two games and five total in Miami's other three tilts, and he's topped 37 yards just once in five games. The Jets have been stingy against the position, allowing just one touchdown, though they have allowed 44 or more yards in three straight weeks. Miami's limited passing game further adds doubt to Dulcich's viability.

free_agents.name: Kyle Williams
free_agents.outlook: Kyle Williams could factor into the Patriots' receiving rotation in Week 7 against the Bears if Romeo Doubs (shoulder) is unable to play. Williams has three or fewer targets in every game to date, but averaging 24.5 yards per catch, he's proven capable of doing more with less. While more volume can be anticipated, Williams will have a chance to stretch the field against a defense that's allowing 9.8 yards per target, the third-highest in the league.

free_agents.name: Bam Knight
free_agents.outlook: Bam Knight got an extended opportunity in the absence of Jeremiyah Love (ankle) in Week 6 against the Rams and made the most of the situation, notching 15 carries for 80 yards and outplaying Tyler Allgeier, who mustered just 38 rushing yards on 18 rushing attempts. It remains to be seen whether Love will be an option in the backfield in Week 7, as much of that will depend on whether Love is cleared to play, but he's a player worth keeping close tabs on in the event Love isn't 100 percent ready. The matchup is favorable on paper, as the Broncos have given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing tailbacks this season.

free_agents.name: Ted Hurst III
free_agents.outlook: Ted Hurst will look to build on a solid Week 6 performance when the Buccaneers' travel to Carolina in Week 7. Hurst was Tampa Bay's second-leading receiver in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, catching three of six targets for 40 yards. While he remains firmly behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin in the Buccaneers' receiving corps, it appears as if he's established himself as the team's No. 3 wideout, at least while Jalen McMillan (knee) remains sidelined. Hurst could also benefit from the possible return of Baker Mayfield (thumb) at quarterback in Week  7, but he'll likely struggle against a Carolina secondary that's allowed just 9.7 yards per completion this year.

free_agents.name: Jacob Cowing
free_agents.outlook: Jacob Cowing and the 49ers travel to square off against the Falcons in Week 7. He did not record a target during San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6, marking his third such outing through six games. Cowing tallied 24 yards on one kickoff return and two yards on one punt return, fumbling once while making the recovery. Even with Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) expected to miss the road tilt with Atlanta, Cowing should not be considered in any fantasy format until he's able to prove otherwise.

free_agents.name: Jason Sanders
free_agents.outlook: Jason Sanders could offer bye-week replacement production for the Jets in a Week 7 meeting with the Dolphins. Sanders drilled a season-high four field goals in Week 6, his third game in six appearances with multiple 3-point connections, and he's added multiple PATs at the same 50% clip. Miami's defense has allowed plenty of points to opposing kickers, surrendering three extra point attempts and two field goals per game, setting Sanders up for a potentially busy, high-scoring Week 7.

free_agents.name: Tommy Tremble
free_agents.outlook: Tommy Tremble will look to stay hot in the Panthers' Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Tremble had his most productive outing of the 2026 season in the Week 6 win over the Eagles, catching all four targets for 46 yards and two touchdowns. Despite this performance, Tremble ranks second amongst Carolina tight ends in targets (18) and yards (128) through six weeks, trailing Darren Waller (21 targets and 148 yards). Tremble could stay productive in Week 7 against a Buccaneers defense that's given up 15.7 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs this season.

free_agents.name: Cole Kmet
free_agents.outlook: Cole Kmet will remain a depth option in Chicago's passing game during Week 7 against New Engand. Kmet recorded two catches for three yards in Week 6 against the Falcons, with one of them being a near trip to the end zone. The veteran tight end has now logged seven catches for 59 yards and a touchdown across six games this season. He'll face a Falcons defense that's ranked top 10 against fantasy TEs this year.
